changed.title: It is false that: Find a six-gate four-row selector with ordered pair and triple witnesses and free column features
changed.statement:
¬ (∃ (G : Fin 4 → Fin 6 → Bool) (code : Fin 6 → Fin 4 → Bool)
    (C : PEqualNP.CircuitLowerBounds.Circuit),
  (∀ u v : Fin 4, u ≠ v → ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G v c = false) ∧
  (∀ u v w : Fin 4, u ≠ v → u ≠ w → v ≠ w →
    ∃ c, G u c = true ∧ G v c = true ∧ G w c = false) ∧
  PEqualNP.MetaComplexity.Monotone2 C ∧ C.size ≤ 6 ∧
  ∀ (u : Fin 4) (c : Fin 6),
    C.eval (List.ofFn (fun i : Fin 4 => decide (i = u)) ++ List.ofFn (code c)) = G u c)
changed.unlocks: Proving it shows that a listed statement is false.
changed.context: The literal negation of another statement of the fleet; a counterexample to that statement proves it.
changed.sketch: Take the alleged four-row, six-column table, its four free column features and its circuit. Specialize the checked row-selector lower bound to n=4, m=6, p=4. The ordered-pair and ordered-triple hypotheses and every one-hot evaluation are supplied by the witness. The bound gives seven gates, contradicting its size of at most six. Four row-feature ANDs joined by three ORs give the seven-gate control using the six unordered row pairs as columns.
